subject: Re: Post-call: OptiNova discovery + model-fit benchmarks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@optinova.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@optinova.ai>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (OptiNova discovery)

Hi Samantha / Raj —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to learn more about OptiNova's QA assistant use case and the latency constraints for internal Slack integrations. Quick recap and next steps: 

- Key requirements: ~99th percentile latency < 350ms on short-turn queries (<=256 tokens), throughput target ~200 TPS across concurrent agents, strong instruction-following on multi-turn context, and deterministic compliance filtering.
- Suggested Redwood starting profile: rwd-gpt-16k-quant-s8 (balanced latency/cost) and rwd-turbo-8k for lower-cost/lightweight scenarios.
- We'll run a focused model-fit evaluation using your sample prompt set (thanks for sending the subset on the call). We'll surface Redwood-verified performance profiles (latency percentiles, p50/p90/p99, and TPS under continuous batching) and per-prompt quality notes.

Deliverables & timing:
1) Benchmark results + Redwood-verified model profiles (link + PDF) — by EOD Wednesday (Nov 11).
2) Full prompt set + recommended prompt templates (attached) — today.
3) Follow-up call to review results and next steps — Thursday, Nov 12. Please confirm a 30-min slot between 10–12 PT.

Attachments: optnova_prompt_set_v2.json (prompt examples / expected outputs)

If that looks correct, I'll kick off the evals and loop in Alex for the performance tuning side.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@optinova.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@optinova.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:18:22 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (OptiNova discovery)

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect. A few clarifications: 

1) For the p99 latency target, is the 350ms expectation for cold-first-token or steady-state (with KV cache)? Our infra skews a bit on short bursts so steady-state p99 is the one that matters.
2) On throughput: 200 TPS is max concurrent; what does Redwood measure for sustained TPS under continuous batching versus peak short-burst TPS?

We can do Thursday 11/12 at 10:30 PT for the follow-up.

— Samantha
Head of Product, OptiNova
Samantha.Liu@optinova.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@optinova.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@optinova.ai>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:04:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (OptiNova discovery)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the quick Qs. Short answers below, and I'm attaching the initial Redwood-verified profiles and prompt set PDF for your review.

1) Latency definition: p99s in our deliverable are "steady-state" p99 measured with warm KV cache and realistic batching (we run the prompt suite with representative session lengths). We also surface first-token cold-starts separately.

2) TPS definitions: we report steady-state sustained TPS (continuous batching profile) and 95th-percentile short-burst TPS. The benchmark PDF includes both charts — the key is that rwd-gpt-16k-quant-s8 hits ~220 sustained TPS with median latency ~120ms and p99 ~310ms on our Dedicated 4xA100 config using your prompt mix. rwd-turbo-8k is cheaper (lower cost per token) but lower sustained TPS (~140) and p99 ~420ms on the same hardware.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_optinova_20261110.pdf, model_profiles_redwood_verified.csv

I'll have Alex run a quick cost/latency tradeoff pass to recommend a default config for your SLAs — looping him in.

Cheers,
Marissa

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@optinova.ai>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@optinova.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (OptiNova discovery)

Hi Samantha — good to meet you (virtually) — quick technical notes on the benchmarks and config suggestions: 

- The numbers Marissa shared are for our Dedicated 4xA100 profile with batching tuned to your request distribution. The p99 ~310ms is steady-state with KV caching enabled and a 128-token context window for embeddings/prefix paths.
- Cold-first-token p99s are typically ~120–150ms higher depending on model variant; we include that column in model_profiles_redwood_verified.csv.
- Recommendation: start with rwd-gpt-16k-quant-s8 pinned for production; enable a fallback route to rwd-turbo-8k for background or lower-SLA traffic to save cost. We can tune request-level routing by route tag (e.g., slack-internal vs. external) to preserve user-facing latency.

I'll also set up an eval run (same prompt set) on a slightly higher quantization to compare cost vs. p99 impact and share a one-page tradeoff doc by EOD.

— Alex
Principal Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@optinova.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@optinova.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (OptiNova discovery)

Thanks team — confirmed for 10:30 PT. The benchmark PDF looks good; we'll review the CSV tonight and flag any quality/regression concerns. Two asks before the call: 

1) Can you include a short column in the CSV that maps each prompt ID to a qualitative label (pass / regress / needs-tuning) based on Redwood's eval?
2) If possible, include the raw model outputs for the 25 prompts that failed our internal checks so we can triage faster.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — see you Thursday.

Raj
VP Eng, OptiNova
